title: 2014 HMMT November Guts Problem 15
statement: Carl is on a vertex of a regular pentagon. Every minute, he randomly selects an adjacent vertex (each with probability \(\frac{1}{2}\) ) and walks along the edge to it. What is the probability that after 10 minutes, he ends up where he had started?

solutions.text: \(\frac{127}{512}\) Let A denote a clockwise move and B denote a counterclockwise move. We want to have some combination of 10 A's and B's, with the number of A's and the number of B's differing by a multiple of 5 . We have \(\binom{10}{0}+\binom{10}{5}+\binom{10}{10}=254\). Hence the answer is \(\frac{254}{2^{10}}=\frac{127}{512}\).
